svg.title: Closest approach of every Atlantic hurricane to this coast, 1851 to 2024
svg.desc: A polar chart. The cross at the centre is the stretch of north coast where the land sits. Each dot is one Atlantic storm at the moment it came closest while still at hurricane strength, placed at its true bearing and distance and coloured by Saffir-Simpson category. Rings mark 25, 50, 100 and 150 kilometres. In 174 years of records no hurricane-strength system has entered the 25 kilometre ring, and nineteen of the twenty-four passed to the north of the coast.
